name: [Part 1] Empty and out-of-order timestamps
test:
p = CommodityPrices()
assert p.max_price() is None
assert p.get_price(10, 0) is None
assert p.upsert(10, 8) == 1
assert p.upsert(2, 12) == 2
assert p.upsert(8, 5) == 3
assert p.max_price() == 12

name: [Part 1] Correcting the maximum can lower the answer
test:
p = CommodityPrices()
p.upsert(10, 8)
p.upsert(5, 12)
p.upsert(5, 3)
assert p.max_price() == 8
p.upsert(10, 1)
assert p.max_price() == 3
p.upsert(10, 20)
assert p.max_price() == 20

name: [Part 2] Inclusive checkpoints preserve corrected values
test:
p = CommodityPrices()
assert p.upsert(10, 8) == 1
assert p.upsert(5, 12) == 2
assert p.upsert(5, 3) == 3
assert p.upsert(5, 7) == 4
assert [p.get_price(5, c) for c in range(5)] == [None, None, 12, 3, 7]
assert [p.get_price(10, c) for c in range(5)] == [None, 8, 8, 8, 8]
assert p.get_price(999, 4) is None

name: [Part 2] Unrelated updates do not reset a timestamp version
test:
p = CommodityPrices()
for t, v in [(4, 5), (1, 9), (4, 2), (1, 6), (8, 11)]:
    p.upsert(t, v)
assert [p.get_price(4, c) for c in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]] == [5, 5, 2, 2, 2]
assert [p.get_price(1, c) for c in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]] == [None, 9, 9, 6, 6]
assert p.max_price() == 11

name: [Both parts] Equal prices, repeated upserts and independent instances
input: duplicate price entries and negative values
test:
p = CommodityPrices()
assert p.upsert(1, -2) == 1
assert p.upsert(2, -2) == 2
assert p.upsert(1, -5) == 3
assert p.max_price() == -2
assert p.upsert(2, -2) == 4
assert p.get_price(1, 2) == -2
assert p.get_price(1, 4) == -5
other = CommodityPrices()
assert other.max_price() is None
assert other.upsert(1, 100) == 1
assert p.max_price() == -2
